title: Hyeonggeun Choe
text:
I am a Ph.D. candidate in Criminology at the University of Pennsylvania, where I am also pursuing a master’s degree in Statistics and Data Science.
My research examines how policing practices and criminal justice interventions shape police behavior and neighborhood violence, with particular emphasis on modern causal inference methods. My work examines a range of topics, including the adoption of body-worn cameras (BWCs), gang takedowns, recreational cannabis legalization, and the relationship between licensed firearm dealers and local gun violence.

text:
2025 Fall: CRIM 5350: Quantitative Methods for Public Policy
I lead weekly lab sessions that help graduate students apply quantitative methods to substantive questions in criminology and public policy. The labs provide hands-on instruction in R, covering data management, visualization, statistical analysis, and the interpretation of empirical results.
I also developed an introductory R primer and supplementary materials to support students with varying levels of prior programming experience. My teaching emphasizes active participation: I identify common difficulties, work through applications interactively, and encourage students to connect statistical concepts to real-world research and policy questions.
